{
    private int $balance = 0;

    public function deposit(int $amount): void

        $this->balance += $amount;

{

    public function bind(string $id, Closure $factory): void
    {
        $this->factories[$id] = $factory;
    }

    public function singleton(string $id, Closure $factory): void
    {

    }

    public function make(string $id): object
    {
        return ($this->factories[$id])();
    }

// Test driver (leave as is): is make() twice the same object?
function sameInstance(bool $useSingleton): bool
{
    $c = new Container();
    $factory = fn () => new stdClass();

coding.referenceSolution:
<?php

class Container
{
    private array $factories = [];

    public function bind(string $id, Closure $factory): void
    {
        $this->factories[$id] = $factory;
    }

    public function singleton(string $id, Closure $factory): void
    {
        $instance = null;
        $this->factories[$id] = function () use (&$instance, $factory) {
            return $instance ??= $factory();
        };
    }

    public function make(string $id): object
    {
        return ($this->factories[$id])();
    }
}

function sameInstance(bool $useSingleton): bool
{
    $c = new Container();
    $factory = fn () => new stdClass();
    $useSingleton ? $c->singleton('cache', $factory) : $c->bind('cache', $factory);
    return $c->make('cache') === $c->make('cache');
}

coding.referenceSolution:
<?php

final class Email
{
    public readonly string $value;

    public function __construct(string $value)
    {
        $value = strtolower(trim($value));
        if (!filter_var($value, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL)) {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException("Invalid email: $value");

        $this->value = $value;
    }

    public function equals(Email $other): bool
    {
        return $this->value === $other->value;
    }
}

function sameEmail(string $a, string $b): string
{
    try {
        return (new Email($a))->equals(new Email($b)) ? 'same' : 'different';
    } catch (InvalidArgumentException $e) {
        return 'invalid';
    }
}

coding.referenceSolution:
<?php

class Dispatcher
{
    private array $listeners = [];

    public function listen(string $event, callable $listener, int $priority = 0): void
    {
        $this->listeners[$event][] = ['fn' => $listener, 'priority' => $priority];
    }

    public function dispatch(string $event): array
    {
        $listeners = $this->listeners[$event] ?? [];
        usort($listeners, fn ($a, $b) => $b['priority'] <=> $a['priority']);
        $results = [];
        foreach ($listeners as $l) {
            $results[] = ($l['fn'])();
        }
        return $results;
    }
}

function dispatchLog(array $listeners, string $event): array
{
    $d = new Dispatcher();
    foreach ($listeners as [$name, $priority, $label]) {
        $d->listen($name, fn () => $label, $priority);
    }
    return $d->dispatch($event);
}

class Pipeline

    private array $stages = [];

    public function then(string $input, Closure $destination): string

coding.referenceSolution:
<?php

interface RateProvider
{
    public function rate(string $currency): float;
}

class SlowProvider implements RateProvider
{
    public int $calls = 0;

    public function rate(string $currency): float
    {
        $this->calls++;
        return strlen($currency) / 10;
    }
}

class CachedRates implements RateProvider
{
    private array $cache = [];

    public function __construct(private RateProvider $inner) {}

    public function rate(string $currency): float
    {
        return $this->cache[$currency] ??= $this->inner->rate($currency);
    }
}

function providerCalls(array $currencies): int
{
    $slow = new SlowProvider();
    $rates = new CachedRates($slow);
    foreach ($currencies as $c) {
        $rates->rate($c);
    }
    return $slow->calls;
}

coding.referenceSolution:
<?php

final class Money
{
    public function __construct(public readonly int $amount, public readonly string $currency) {}

    public function add(Money $other): Money
    {
        if ($other->currency !== $this->currency) {
            throw new DomainException('currency mismatch');
        }
        return new Money($this->amount + $other->amount, $this->currency);
    }
}

function addMoney(array $a, array $b): array|string
{
    try {
        $sum = (new Money(...$a))->add(new Money(...$b));
        return ['amount' => $sum->amount, 'currency' => $sum->currency];
    } catch (DomainException $e) {
        return 'error: ' . $e->getMessage();
    }
}

coding.referenceSolution:
<?php

class QueryBuilder
{
    public array $wheres = [];

    public function __call(string $method, array $args): static
    {
        if (str_starts_with($method, 'where')) {
            $column = strtolower(preg_replace('/(?<!^)[A-Z]/', '_$0', substr($method, 5)));
            $this->wheres[] = [$column, $args[0]];
            return $this;
        }
        throw new BadMethodCallException("Method $method does not exist.");
    }
}

function buildWheres(array $calls): array
{
    $q = new QueryBuilder();
    foreach ($calls as [$method, $value]) {
        $q->$method($value);
    }
    return $q->wheres;
}

coding.referenceSolution:
<?php

enum Role: string
{
    case Admin = 'admin';
    case Editor = 'editor';
    case Viewer = 'viewer';

    public function permissions(): array
    {
        return match ($this) {
            self::Admin => ['*'],
            self::Editor => ['view', 'edit', 'publish'],
            self::Viewer => ['view'],
        };
    }

    public function can(string $permission): bool
    {
        $perms = $this->permissions();
        return in_array('*', $perms, true) || in_array($permission, $perms, true);
    }
}

function rolesThatCan(string $permission): array
{
    $roles = array_filter(Role::cases(), fn (Role $r) => $r->can($permission));
    return array_values(array_map(fn (Role $r) => $r->value, $roles));
}

prompt: `PdfReport` and `CsvReport` share how data is loaded and filtered, but differ only in how the result is written out. More formats are coming. Which design keeps this easiest to extend and test?

options: One `Report` class that receives a `ReportWriter` interface (strategy); each format is a small writer class
A trait per format, all used by the same `Report` class
mcq.explanation: The varying part (the writer) sits behind an interface and is injected, so a new format is a new class, not a change to `Report`, and each writer can be tested alone. Deep inheritance couples formats to the loading code, a `switch` must be edited for every format, and traits mixed into one class collide.
